description: Run by .github/workflows/renovate.yml (self-hosted, once a day after the server and player releases, RENOVATE_TOKEN), not by the Mend GitHub App.

No pull requests, no waiting: automergeType branch plus ignoreTests means an automerged bump is pushed as a renovate/* branch and fast-forwarded into main in the same run. Nothing tests the branch itself -- the release (release.yml) runs the full CI on main before it publishes, so a bad bump fails the release rather than ships. Third-party majors keep automerge:false and still open a PR; first-party (ghcr.io/ister-app) majors automerge too.

packageRules.description: Third-party images: automerge patches only. A minor bump of Postgres, RabbitMQ or Typesense is a real upgrade of a stateful component, so it gets a human.

GitHub Actions, plus ci.yml's HELM_VERSION through the custom manager below. Grouped, and chore(deps) rather than fix(deps) so a bumped action does not release a new chart -- .github/ is not among the paths release.yml diffs. Needs the RENOVATE_TOKEN PAT with the workflow scope: GITHUB_TOKEN may not push changes under .github/workflows/.

Third-party majors are never automerged, actions included (a helm 4 in the release workflow is not a patch). They land on the dependency dashboard and wait for a human. Rules apply in order: this sits after the actions rule so it overrides its automerge, and before the first-party rule below, which overrides this one.

First-party ister images: every server or player release, majors included, becomes a chart release -- the chart pins them independently and the release e2e is the gate, so a first-party major that needs a chart change fails the release (and blocks the following ones) until the chart catches up. Each image gets its own branch and its own version line; server, player and migrations do not move in lockstep.

customManagers.description: ci.yml pins helm in an env var, which no manager reads: the actions manager only sees the setup-helm version input in release.yml, so a bump moved the packaging helm and left the tested one behind. The rule above puts this in the actions group; a major still falls through to the majors rule and opens a PR.
